findings.title: Escape Velocity – comfort-seeking through cuteification, toys and fandoms
findings.description: Faced with economic pressure and anxiety, adults (especially Gen Z & Millennials) are escaping into ‘dystopian cuteness’, collectibles and immersive fandoms. 63 % say cute packaging brings joy and 36 % define themselves by their fandoms.
findings.evidence: “Adults are turning to toys for comfort in record numbers… Consumers are embracing soft toys, charms, and collectibles”

findings.title: Electric Dreams – deepening emotional ties to AI & backlash against ‘slop’ content
findings.description: AI is becoming an emotional companion: 32 % of Gen Z/Millennials feel their AI chatbot understands them better than friends/family, while only 46 % feel confident spotting AI content. Simultaneously, hyper-realistic AI influencers raise copyright and authenticity dilemmas.
findings.evidence: “I sometimes feel my AI chatbot understands me better than my friends and family” – 32 % agree overall (rising to 46 % Millennials, 42 % Gen Z)

findings.title: Trad Lives – grounding in nature, locality & spirituality
findings.description: Consumers seek certainty and connection to the land: 75 % globally are drawn to spending more time in nature and 64 % to traditional values. Spiritual engagement is surging; UK church attendance among 16-24-year-olds has quadrupled since 2018.
findings.evidence: “Consumers the world over exhibit a yearning to touch grass and root their hands in the soil”

findings.title: Alone Together – reinventing ‘third spaces’ & natural highs
findings.description: Rising loneliness drives demand for new social formats (morning raves, chess clubs) and low/no-alcohol ‘natural highs’. Only 54 % of US adults now identify as drinkers, fuelling a boom in NoLo spirits and inclusive venues like Asahi’s SUMADORI bars.
findings.evidence: “Loneliness and isolation are on the rise … consumers are seeking new ‘third spaces’ as the no/low-alcohol trend means pubs are no longer the default hangout”

findings.title: Analog Futures – neo-Luddite pushback against the algorithm
findings.description: Younger consumers are experimenting with pre-digital living and tactile rituals; 47 % of UK 16-21-year-olds wish they’d grown up in a pre-internet era. Start-ups like Brick and KARRI remove smartphone distractions, while retro devices (Walkman-style MP3s) resurface.
findings.evidence: “In response to an online world that feels less safe and inclusive, many younger consumers are exploring more analog approaches”
